content:
Manchester United confirmed the arrival of Manuel Ugarte from Paris Saint‑Germain in a €50m deal that could rise by €10m with bonuses, the Uruguay international signing a five‑year contract with an option for an extra season. At 23, he steps into Erik ten Hag’s midfield as a ball‑winning anchor, complementing Casemiro and offering the manager greater flexibility in big games.

Ugarte spoke with visible excitement about the scale of the club and the expectations that come with it. He described a project that aligns with his own hunger: bring intensity back to the center of the pitch, set a higher standard in training, and help turn narrow matches into routine wins. Teammates say his first sessions showed relentless pressing, crisp distribution off one and two touches, and a willingness to marshal others—traits the staff believe will free creative players to thrive.

Behind the scenes, recruitment chiefs had tracked Ugarte for months, convinced his reading of danger and ability to spring transitions would mesh with Ten Hag’s structure. The manager wants a more aggressive press, quicker recoveries after turnovers, and a reliable screen in front of the back line; Ugarte’s blend of timing and tenacity was considered essential. While he will need to adapt to the Premier League’s rhythm, the early plan is straightforward: rotate with Casemiro, or play alongside him in high‑stakes fixtures to lock down the middle third.

United’s leaders view the signing as another building block in a summer focused on clarity: clearer roles, clearer recruitment, clearer identity. Supporters, meanwhile, are eager to see how Ugarte’s bite and composure translate under the lights at Old Trafford. If his words match his performances, he could become the heartbeat of a side determined to rejoin Europe’s elite. Any other questions?
